methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective single-center cohort design (n=298, 2000–2022) is appropriate for external validation of an existing prognostic score, and the use of competing-risks analysis for recurrence versus non-recurrence death (Section 2.6; Table 4) is a methodological strength. However, the exclusion criteria sentence is truncated in Section 2.1 ('Patients were excluded from this study in case of'), leaving selection unclear. No sample size/power calculation is reported, no C-statistic or calibration plot is provided for the validated model, and handling of missing data is not described. The uneven distribution across RETREAT categories (only 29 high-risk patients; scores 5 and 6 contain only 9 and 4 patients) limits the precision of HR estimates for the high-risk class, and the authors concede era-stratified sensitivity analyses were not feasible despite 22 years of evolving practice.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study validating an established prognostic score, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is moderate: the endpoints (HCC recurrence, overall survival) are patient-relevant, and the stratification could plausibly inform post-LT surveillance intensity and immunosuppression tailoring in a European real-world setting. However, the score depends on explant pathology, limiting pre-LT allocation utility, and no interventional implication is tested—the authors explicitly frame adjuvant/surveillance proposals as 'hypothesis-generating' in the Conclusions.

reporting_quality.justification: As a validation of a prediction model, TRIPOD is the applicable checklist. The manuscript reports population, predictors, and outcome definitions reasonably well (Sections 2.1–2.5) and distinguishes derivation from validation context, but omits key TRIPOD items: no discrimination statistic (C-index/AUROC) with CI, no calibration plot or Hosmer–Lemeshow, no participant flow diagram, no handling of missing predictors, and the exclusion criteria are truncated. Protocol/registration is not described beyond local ethics approval. No data-sharing or code-availability statement is present in the blinded text; the SPSS/R analysis is noted but no scripts are referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is an incremental external validation of the RETREAT score (Mehta 2017), which has already been validated in multiple prior cohorts the authors themselves cite (refs 18–21: Dutch, European multicenter, UNOS, UK). The claimed novelty is the Italian single-center setting, the 22-year span, and the use of competing-risks analysis, plus an exploratory RETREAT+ modification adding tumor grade—which the authors concede did not improve predictive performance over the original score. No new mechanism, new biomarker, or new modeling approach is introduced; the contribution is empirical confirmation in a new geographic cohort.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with clear section structure and an informative abstract that aligns quantitatively with the Results. However, Section 2.1 contains a truncated/unfinished sentence defining the exclusion criteria, and Section 2.6 contains an incomplete bracket ('R (version 4.5.2 [REDACTED]'). The Discussion is repetitive—restating RETREAT's strengths and the study's three/four 'contributions' across multiple paragraphs—and could be tightened. Figures are referenced appropriately but captions are not available in the blinded text for independent assessment.

key_strengths: Appropriate use of competing-risks analysis for recurrence versus non-recurrence death, strengthening causal interpretation of HRs
Large single-center cohort (n=298) with long median follow-up (64 months) covering up to 15 years post-LT
Clinically meaningful stratification: 5-year RFS of 93%/78%/58% across RETREAT low/medium/high groups (p<0.001) with HRs of 2.3 and 6.4 versus low-risk
Captures real-world evolution across Milan and Up-to-Seven eras and down-staging strategies in a European setting
key_concerns: Truncated exclusion-criteria sentence in Methods (Section 2.1) leaves cohort selection ambiguous
No C-statistic, calibration plot, or formal discrimination metric reported for a validation study—core TRIPOD items missing
Very small high-risk subgroups (score 5 n=9, score 6 n=4) make HR estimates imprecise and preclude era-stratified sensitivity analyses the authors acknowledge are missing
Novelty is incremental: at least four prior external validations of RETREAT (refs 18–21) are cited, and the RETREAT+ modification did not outperform the original
No power calculation, no missing-data handling description, no data/code availability statement
Discussion is repetitive and partially restates results rather than contextualizing them
chief_reviewer.rationale: The paper is a competent but incremental single-center external validation of an already widely validated prognostic score, with solid competing-risks methodology but missing standard prediction-model performance metrics (discrimination, calibration) and truncated methods text. It fits a tier-4 oncology journal with minor revisions to repair the Methods, add C-statistic/calibration, and tighten the Discussion.
